summary: Nobunaga Takasa specializes in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at National Institute of Technology, Sendai College (attested 1991) and as a researcher at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a researcher (attested 1995).

Nobuyoshi Yamabe studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Osaka University under Noritoshi Aramaki and earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Agriculture (~2003–2015) and Waseda University (~2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University (~1956–1964). His career included posts at Nagoya University, Osaka University (~1973–1999), and Doshisha University (~1999–2006), alongside affiliations at Koyasan and Ritsumeikan universities.

Nobuyuki Watase specializes in Indology. He completed master's studies at Kyoto University (~1964–1968) and taught at Tokai University as an assistant professor (~1978–1988) and professor (~1988–2011).

Nobuyuki Yoshimoto studied Buddhist studies at Otani University (~1960–1969) under Genjun Sasaki and Issai Funahashi. He served as a JSPS researcher (1972) and held lecturer and research positions at Otani University (~1982–2006).

Norbert M. Samuelson was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Northwestern, Hebrew Union College, and Indiana University, later holding a post at Arizona State University (~1998–2018).

Noriaki Hakamaya studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He spent his career primarily at Komazawa University as lecturer and professor (~1972–2013), and also taught at Komazawa Junior College (~1993–2001).
Noriaki Hosoda specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held positions at Hokkaido University as an assistant (attested 1986) and assistant professor (attested 2003).
Noriaki Inoue is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University (~1949–1953), where he later served as a professor (attested 1982).
Norihiko Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Osaka Kyoiku University (~1964–1968) and served as a professor at Bukkyo University (~1990–2015).
Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. In 1962, he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies and the University of Tokyo.

Norihisa Baba studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo (Ph.D. ~1998–2003). He served as an associate professor at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (~2010–2020).

Norio Koyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Shinshu University (~1979–1983) under Seitatsu Matsunami and later served as a professor at Taisho University (attested 2014).

Noritoshi Aramaki studied Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology at Kyoto University (~1955–1964). He held professorships at Osaka University (~1981–1986), Kyoto University (~1986–2000; emeritus ~2000), and Otani University (~2000–2007).

Noriyuki Kudo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed postgraduate studies at Bukkyo University. He served as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2020) and editor-in-chief at the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (attested 2002–2012).
Norvin Hein was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Franklin Edgerton. He served as an associate professor of comparative religion at Yale Divinity School (attested 1965).

Nosei Fuji studied Buddhist studies at Dongguk University (1986). He directed the Buddhist Cultural Institute at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007) and served as professor of Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He was associate director at the NCC Center for the Study of Japanese Religions (1974) and held a post at the University of Oslo (~1986–2011).

Noémie Verdon is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Lausanne (–2015) under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, and later held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2019).
